# Independent audit: joint penalized physical dual and logarithmic reserve

Target: `candidate 8ab518b2afa5de5c`,
Sections 1--8 including the surface contact and zero-reserve additions.

signed-direction scope. No correction found. This is an analytic audit;
no new numerical optimization or unprovided verifier is used.

## 1. One physically valid separator

For a bounded signed radial body direction and an arbitrary affine phi,
the positive unnormalized parameter ell+t phi can be geometrically
renormalized using the ACTUAL changing masses. Both signs of phi are
locally feasible. The signed complete-cut theorem supplies finite addition
of the chosen actual body speeds. Regular cap responses are linear in
those speeds; this would fail at supporting caps and is correctly not
asserted there.

Therefore the joint finite response vectors form a convex cone, including
the affine-parameter linear subspace. Absence of an all-strict improving
vector gives ONE nonnegative normalized eta by separation from the open
positive orthant. This does not require closure of the response cone.
Its parameter part vanishes because both signs are feasible. The same eta
then tests every allowed body direction. No minimax swap or unrelated
body/parameter multipliers are used.

## 2. Independent normalization and sign check

Writing w_z=V_z/M and Mdot=-D gives

    wdot_z=(-D_z+w_z D)/M.

Differentiating sum w_z log ell_z=0 under the raw affine perturbation phi
therefore gives

    dot ell_z/ell_z=sum D_z log ell_z/M
                         +phi(z)/ell_z-sum w_z phi(z)/ell_z.

Substitution into dot P for P=sum w ell yields exactly source (2).
The singleton contact bonus is

    delta_i [ C_i/(N E_i)+J_i^cov/(2M)
       -(N+2)D/(2NM)-dot ell_i/(N ell_i) ].

Combining it with the cap loss, -beta D, and the ACTUAL penalty derivative
-M epsilon^2 dot P gives precisely (3), with all its signs.
Testing the parameter part with both signs yields (5). In particular
the penalty term is added to the left side of that equation, not dropped.

Collecting the shape-induced logarithmic scaling and penalty terms gives

    B(z)=epsilon^2(ell_z-P)
               -[Delta/(NM)+epsilon^2 P] log ell_z.

Thus the density (7), including its constant -(N+2)Delta/(2NM), is exact.
Its volume-weighted mean is zero and its base Hessian has the printed
positive sign. These statements do not imply a surface-weighted sign.
The two-fiber sign and unequal-perimeter calibrations correctly retain
this distinction.

## 3. Active-source balance and anchored reserve

Equation (10) is an equality of mass and first base moment only. Its
constant test gives a strictly positive mass for nu/ell, and its first
moment gives the extrapolated barycenter (11). Affineness of ell gives
ell(g_vol)=P and ell(g_tilt)=1/Z. Hence

    ell(h)=a/(kappa Z-epsilon^2).

For a nonconstant positive sampled ell, P>1 and Z>1. The strict comparison
ell(h)<1/Z is exactly epsilon^2(PZ-1)>0. Thus the conclusion that some
positive-weight active source has ell<1 is valid, with its actual eta
weights retained.

On an anchored base relation the affine part of B cancels, leaving the
Jensen gap for -log. Its strong-convexity constant on the finite positive
range is 1/ell_max^2, proving (13)--(14) including the equality criterion.
There is no conclusion yet that this reserve has a favorable global size.

## 4. Surface Jordan marginals and contact geometry

Every finite continuous signed convex PHYSICAL potential is an actual
speed of the signed complete support-cut class, by using the same field
on all complete baseline planes. Thus the full signed convex tests in
(15) are justified by the specified physical cone. The affine tests force
equal Jordan SURFACE mass and first physical moment. The compact convex-
order theorem then gives the martingale from Xi_+ d sigma to Xi_- d sigma.
It is not a martingale of fiber volumes or of the old cap profile.

The tangent continuation of -log below the positive minimum of ell is
a globally finite convex extension agreeing on the whole real base hull.
It is a permitted test. Testing B and using the exact Jordan marginals
gives both (16) and the identity in (17). The affine term cancels under
the conditional martingale mean, and the strong-convexity remainder has
the correct positive sign and factor kappa/(2 ell_max^2).

At a regular source boundary point, the finite support LP has value h_p(u):
actual compatibility bounds every anchored support average by h_p(u),
and the self representation attains equality. The dual affine majorant
is feasible and attained, including at boundary bases. Its nonnegative
physical slack has conditional expectation zero, hence vanishes on targets.
Splitting this slack into its base-support gap and its own-fiber support
gap proves that targets lie on the SAME actual plane and their u-faces.
Their finite base probabilities give exactly the tight anchored identities
(18). The specified continuous normal is nonzero throughout.

No uncountable measurable-selection gap is present. On the full source
set where the vector conditional mean holds, the deterministic affine-
slack argument applies to every supporting plane at that source. Target
nonregular sets are null for the Jordan surface marginal.

## 5. Exact scope of zero reserve

Let R be the nonnegative quantity in (17). If, additionally, R=0, strict
convexity of -log forces ell(target)=ell(source) on every martingale edge
almost surely. The coupling decomposes by the finitely many sampled ell
levels. Each level separately has equal Jordan mass and first physical
moment and satisfies convex order. If ell is injective on P, this gives
fiberwise convex order WITHOUT assuming independent fiber mobility.
The planar boundary face decomposition can then be applied on each fiber.

This is a legitimate conditional strengthening. Neither stationarity,
volume centering of B, nor the affine-moment identity proves R=0. The
old-part correlation remains on the right side of (16)--(17) and may fund
both the square of B and cross-level transport.

For distinct levels separated by gap>0, the bound (19) follows by charging
every cross-level edge at least gap^2 in the quadratic remainder. A union
of full level blocks has Jordan mass imbalance at most the crossing
transport mass. These are SURFACE statements, not original-volume quotas.

The source makes all these distinctions explicitly. It does not settle
supporting allocations, multiple contacts, or general OC payment.
